title: Grade 10 Science — Chemical Reactions and Equations
description: Types of chemical reactions, balancing equations, and their characteristics
subject: science

questions.question: A chemical equation is balanced to satisfy:
options: The Law of Conservation of Mass — atoms cannot be created or destroyed
questions.explanation: The Law of Conservation of Mass: total mass of reactants = total mass of products. So the number of atoms of each element must be equal on both sides. Hence equations must be balanced.

questions.question: In a combination reaction, two or more substances combine to form:
questions.explanation: Combination (synthesis) reaction: A + B → AB. Example: CaO + H₂O → Ca(OH)₂ (slaked lime). The reactants combine to give a single product.

questions.question: Decomposition reaction is the reverse of combination. Which type of energy is often needed?
options: Heat (thermal), light (photolytic), or electricity (electrolytic) — to break down a compound
questions.explanation: Decomposition: AB → A + B. Types: thermal (CaCO₃ →heat→ CaO + CO₂), photolytic (2AgBr →light→ 2Ag + Br₂), electrolytic (H₂O →electricity→ H₂ + O₂).

questions.question: In a displacement reaction, a more reactive element displaces a less reactive element. Which is correct?
options: Copper displaces zinc from ZnSO₄ solution
Zinc displaces copper from CuSO₄ solution: Zn + CuSO₄ → ZnSO₄ + Cu
Iron displaces gold from AuCl₃ solution
questions.explanation: Zn + CuSO₄ → ZnSO₄ + Cu. Zinc is more reactive than copper (higher in activity series), so it displaces copper from copper sulphate solution. The blue CuSO₄ solution becomes colourless.

questions.question: Double displacement reactions involve:
options: One element replacing another in a compound
Exchange of ions between two compounds to form new compounds (often producing a precipitate)
One reactant breaking into two products
Two elements combining to form one product
questions.explanation: Double displacement: AB + CD → AD + CB. Example: BaCl₂ + Na₂SO₄ → BaSO₄↓ + 2NaCl. Barium sulphate (BaSO₄) precipitates. Also called precipitation reactions when a precipitate forms.

questions.question: The rusting of iron is an example of:
options: Combination (oxidation) reaction — iron reacts with oxygen and moisture
questions.explanation: Rusting: 4Fe + 3O₂ + 6H₂O → 4Fe(OH)₃ → 2Fe₂O₃·3H₂O (rust). Iron is oxidised (gains oxygen). This is a slow combination/oxidation reaction requiring both oxygen AND water.

questions.question: Oxidation and reduction ALWAYS occur together — this is called:
questions.explanation: Redox reactions: oxidation (loss of electrons/gain of oxygen) and reduction (gain of electrons/loss of oxygen) always occur together. One substance is oxidised while another is reduced.

questions.question: Rancidity of food (fats going stale) is prevented by:
options: Using nitrogen gas atmosphere, antioxidants, or refrigeration — prevents oxidation of fats
questions.explanation: Rancidity occurs when fats/oils are oxidised, producing foul taste and smell. Prevention: nitrogen/vacuum packing (removes oxygen), antioxidants (BHA, BHT), refrigeration (slows oxidation), airtight containers.

questions.question: Balance the equation: Fe + O₂ → Fe₂O₃. The balanced form is:
questions.explanation: 4Fe + 3O₂ → 2Fe₂O₃. Check: Left: 4 Fe, 6 O. Right: 4 Fe (2×2), 6 O (2×3). Balanced. ✓

questions.question: Thermite reaction (Fe₂O₃ + 2Al → Al₂O₃ + 2Fe) is an example of:
questions.explanation: Thermite reaction: Aluminium (more reactive) displaces iron from iron oxide. It is a highly exothermic displacement reaction that produces temperatures over 2500°C — used in welding railway tracks.

questions.question: The symbol ↓ in a chemical equation indicates:
questions.explanation: ↓ (downward arrow after formula) = precipitate — an insoluble solid formed in a solution. ↑ = gas evolved. ⇌ = reversible reaction. State symbols: (s), (l), (g), (aq) are more precise.

questions.question: Photosynthesis can be written as: 6CO₂ + 6H₂O → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂. This is a type of:
options: Combination/Synthesis reaction (light energy converts CO₂ and water into glucose)
questions.explanation: Photosynthesis is an endothermic combination reaction — CO₂ and H₂O combine (using light energy from the sun) to form glucose (C₆H₁₂O₆) and oxygen. Energy is absorbed, not released.

questions.question: Exothermic reactions are those that:
questions.explanation: Exothermic reactions release energy: combustion (burning), neutralisation, respiration, thermite reaction. Endothermic reactions absorb energy: photosynthesis, decomposition of CaCO₃.

questions.question: When silver chloride (AgCl) is exposed to sunlight, it turns grey/black. This is because:
options: AgCl reacts with oxygen in air
questions.explanation: Photolytic decomposition: 2AgCl →light→ 2Ag + Cl₂. Silver (grey-black) is deposited. This reaction is used in black-and-white photography. AgBr has the same property.

questions.question: Which of the following is a neutralisation reaction?
questions.explanation: Neutralisation: acid + base → salt + water. NaOH (base) + HCl (acid) → NaCl (salt) + H₂O. It is also a double displacement reaction. The pH of the product is near neutral.
